analysis_objective: Mathematical frontier audit of two-path budget allocations under integer capacity constraint

firm_28.budget_dilemma: To capture Firm 28, Path B requires Kb >= 35 alerts, which alone exceeds the entire cohort cap of 20 alerts!

firm_60.budget_dilemma: Firm 60 is reachable at Kb >= 16, but consumes 16 of the 20 available alert slots.

formal_mathematical_proof: Theorem: Under the strict 8% alert budget constraint (Cap = 20 alerts), no partitioned allocation (Ka, Kb) or score-ranking blend of Path A and Path B can capture Firm 28. Proof: Path B ranks Firm 28 at rank 35 with probability 0.0858. Path A ranks Firm 28 at rank 51 with probability 0.0496. Since rank_B(28) = 35 > 20 and rank_A(28) = 51 > 20, any top-K selection where K <= 20 strictly excludes Firm 28. To include Firm 28, the coordinator must expand the alert budget to at least 35 alerts (an alert rate of 13.36%), breaching the regulatory cap by +15 alerts.
